transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-14 10:30 PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood CSM); Jordan Lee (NovaGrid Head of Platform), Maya Patel (SRE), Eli Turner (FinOps), Hana Okafor (Security)

Summary:
Quick QBR-style checkin focused on pilot economics, reliability incidents from last month, and governance (security artifacts + residency). Customer asked for a 30-day pilot extension while they finish internal exec approval; Redwood proposed mitigations (canary routes, dedicated guards) and offered to run a targeted latency benchmark on customer traffic. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics:
- Usage and cost trends (7% week-over-week increase in inference traffic)
- Recent tail-latency spikes during batch re-ingestion
- Pilot-extension commercial terms and SLA
- Security artifact handoff (SOC2, ISO, audit logs, KMS integration)
- Roadmap items relevant to NovaGrid: autoscale policy controls, prefix-KV cache improvements

Action items (brief): see metadata + note to attach benchmark template and pricing sheet.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): All right, hey everyone thanks for joining. um, Jordan, Maya, thanks for making time. quick agenda: usage, incidents, pricing ask for the pilot ext, and security handoff.
[00:18] Jordan (NovaGrid): Yeah thanks, Alex. I'll hand over to Maya for the SRE summary, I pulled some of the logs into the dashboard but she can speak to the spikes.
[00:28] Maya (SRE): Cool, yeah so we saw two tail spikes last week that correlated to our user-import job hitting an unusual token distribution. It pushed p95 from ~240ms to 820ms for a ~7 minute window, so customer-facing latency was degraded. threw alerts to our pager.
[00:42] Priya (Redwood SE): Right, I saw those in the traces; looks like a sustained sequence length shift and the request fan-out increased. On our side the runtime moved some requests onto the burst pool which added cold-KV cache warms. We suggested at the time an autoscale bump but I want to talk about caching changes.
[01:03] Maya: Yeah we did the temporary autoscale, but the symptom was tail jitter, not total throughput. We think the K V cash warm is the culprit, we call it K V cash, ha, so warm up cost.
[01:16] Priya: (laughs) yep K V cash. So a couple options: increase prefix cache retention for that route, or pin a small dedicated corridor (dedicated capacity) for the import flow. Both have cost tradeoffs.
[01:31] Eli (FinOps): cost-wise we saw the bill jump about 18% month-over-month aligned to that spike window; if we pin dedicated it sounds like an uplift. What are ballpark numbers?
[01:44] Alex: For a short-term dedicated corridor for import flows you'd see a ~12-18% uplift on the service line, but you get predictable tail latency. Alternative is to keep hosted + change cache policy which is lower cost but some risk. We can scope a hybrid rule: prefix cache for imports + strict canary so you don't impact others.
[02:05] Jordan: Our ask — exec wants a 30-day extension on the pilot while they get final signoff. They want an SLA addendum and a clearer runbook for incidents.
[02:17] Diego (Redwood CSM): We can do a 30-day extension. We propose: (1) an SLA addendum with a p95 target and a breach credit tier, (2) run targeted benchmarks with your test harness, and (3) a joint runbook we co-author for import flows.
[02:36] Jordan: That sounds reasonable. We'd like the SLA to include automatic fallback to a lower-capacity model if the primary variant throttles, so user flows don't hard-fail.
[02:50] Priya: We support model fallback policies; we can configure a lightweight lower-cost variant with faster cold-start characteristics as the fallback. There is some quality tradeoff but it prevents full failure.
[03:05] Hana (Security): Quick security note: we'll need SOC2 Type II artifacts, ISO evidentiary lists, and proof of KMS integration. Also need to verify audit log retention and whether Redwood exposes token-level masking in logs.
[03:20] Alex: Good callout. We'll share the security artifacts package and a checklist. Diego will coordinate the SSO/SAML and KMS notes.
[03:28] Hana: Also residency: we need to confirm model weights never leave our VPC when using Redwood Private. For hosted we're ok if data doesn't persist, but the exec will push for private after pilot.
[03:42] Priya: Yep for NovaGrid we already scoped a Private deployment design in the previous doc; I can re-send the network topology and highlight the KMS/HSM flows. For hosted we'd keep everything ephemeral and opt-in to forward-only logging.
[04:00] Jordan: On the benchmark — what metrics will you run?
[04:06] Priya: We'll run p50/p95/p99 latency, tail jitter, throughput, token cost, and cold-start frequency with your sample traffic. We'll also run a failure-injection where we simulate the import fan-out to reproduce warm KV behaviors.
[04:22] Jordan: Good. Eli can you comment on cost guardrails we should accept for the pilot ext?
[04:29] Eli: Ideally we want spending bounded. a soft cap where we get notifications at 80% and hard throttle at 120% of the current pilot run rate. Also want a cost-rollback clause if month burn exceeds projections.
[04:43] Diego: We can set usage alerts and a soft throttle policy; hard throttle is trickier because we don't want to risk breaking customer flows, but can be added as an emergency action with manual approval.
[04:57] Jordan: OK. Can Redwood share a sample annex that lays this out?
[05:02] Alex: Yes — Alex: we'll send a pilot extension annex + pricing. Diego will own the runbook draft. Priya will run the benchmark.
[05:15] Maya: For the incident root-cause, any immediate config change we should make?
[05:20] Priya: Short-term: increase prefix cache retention to 45s for the import route and enable aggressive prefetch for that route. Medium-term: tune the kernel selection for those sequence length distributions — that's a runtime patch but we can push a config change to prefer lower-latency kernels for that traffic.
[05:41] Maya: Will that require a model-restart or rolling deploy?
[05:45] Priya: Rolling deploy, no full restart. We can coordinate a low-traffic window.
[05:52] Hana: On encryption: we need to confirm customer-supplied keys (bring your own key) support for the private offer and also whether hosted supports envelope encryption to the HSM.
[06:03] Alex: We support BYOK for Private and envelope for hosted; we'll share the KMS integration notes in the security packet.
[06:12] Eli: Also, for forecasting: can Redwood give a delta on token cost if we shift to 8-bit quantized model? Ballpark?
[06:20] Priya: Quantization to 8-bit usually reduces token cost ~20-35% depending on model; may add slight degrade to generate quality on edge cases. We'll include model-specific numbers in the benchmark.
[06:35] Jordan: Competitors asked about cost — we've had charters ping VertexAI pricing; can Redwood show a side-by-side?
[06:43] Alex: We'll provide a comparativesheet. Quick note: direct apples-to-apples is tricky because of different token accounting and cached prefixes, but we can show normalized per-request cost under your traffic profile.
[06:58] Maya: One more ops ask: can we get sticky routing guarantee for the import requests to avoid cross-pod fan-out?
[07:06] Priya: Yes — session affinity rules can be applied for a route. It will reduce cross-pod memory churn; another small cost but helps tail.
[07:16] Jordan: Great. Moving to roadmap items — are there any near-term platform features that would help us?
[07:23] Alex: Two items: (1) autoscale policy UI controls for per-route burst thresholds (we plan that on next quarter); (2) prefix-KV cache persisting across restarts (experimental this quarter). Priya, add timeline?
[07:34] Priya: The UI controls are slated for Q1 2028 beta. Prefix persistence is an engineering spike now; we might have an early alpha in Jan. I'll add you to the feature list.
[07:45] Jordan: Ok that maps. If prefix persistence lands we might de-prioritize dedicated corridor.
[07:52] Diego: I'll note the dependency in the runbook.
[07:56] Hana: For audit logs — need retention options for 1 year, 3 years, and an export to their SIEM. Is that available?
[08:05] Alex: Yes, we can configure retention tiers. Exports to S3 or direct syslog to SIEM are both supported; we'll share the doc.
[08:14] Eli: On the billing side — is there a way to get per-route cost breakdown by token and infra so we can allocate to product teams?
[08:22] Diego: Our console has token-level breakdown and per-route cost, with exports. We can set a daily report to send CSV.
[08:30] Jordan: Sounds good. Any other blockers?
[08:33] Maya: Only that we need the benchmark and SLA before the exec meeting. The exec meets next Friday (2027-12-22).
[08:42] Alex: We'll prioritize: Alex to send annex by 12/17, Priya benchmark by 12/20, security sync by 12/22 to satisfy exec.
[08:51] Jordan: Perfect.
[08:54] (background cross-talk)
[09:01] Priya: I'll note that for the benchmark we'll need the NovaGrid test harness credentials and a small sample dataset; please send to sec bucket or to my email.
[09:12] Jordan: I'll get Eli to share the artifacts via secure transfer.
[09:18] Eli: Yep I'll do that after this call.
[09:22] Diego: Quick note on pilot pricing: we can keep the current unit price but extend a commit cap to make it predictable; pricing sheet incoming.
[09:33] Alex: Anything else?
[09:36] Hana: one small ask: can Redwood confirm whether function/tool-calls are logged and redacted for PII? We need that for compliance.
[09:45] Priya: We redact outputs marked as PII and allow masking in logs; we'll include the config options in the security packet.
[09:54] Jordan: OK great, thanks all. Let's recap actions and owners?
[10:00] Diego: Recap: Alex — annex & SLA (12/17). Priya — benchmark (12/20). Diego & Hana — security sync scheduling + artifacts (12/22). Jordan — stakeholder list (12/21). Eli — transfer test harness.
[10:18] Alex: Thanks everyone; we'll follow up in email with attachments.
[10:25] Jordan: Appreciate it. Bye.

End of call.

Notes on transcript quality: some technical terms mistranscribed ("KV cache" as "K V cash"), occasional speaker label flips in auto transcript. We preserved natural speech patterns and filler words.

Referenced documents to attach: pilot-extension-annex-v1.pdf, nova-sample-harness-spec.csv, security-artifacts-pack.zip, benchmark-template.xlsx
